lines.text: CHAPTER
Food on Our Plate
What We Eat and Why It Matters
Sharee
The bell for lunch break rings at Meridian Public School,
and within a minute the corridor smells of six different homes.
Aarav opens his tiffin — lemon rice, still warm.
Ira opens hers — two rotis and a bowl of dal.
From the next bench comes the smell of fish curry,
from the bench behind, of dhokla.
Aarav looks around the room and thinks:
everyone here is eating something different.
Everyone here is hungry at the same time,
and everyone will feel better in ten minutes.
So what is actually happening inside
all those tiffin boxes? Why does food
make us able to run, and think, and grow?
THINK-SPOT
Look at your own lunch today.
Name three things in it.
Where did each one come from?
From where?
